name: Chess
summary: Chess against WOPR. You play White (the capital letters) and move first. WOPR answers with its move as squares, such as WOPR: D7D5.
howToPlay: Checkmate WOPR's king. Stalemate, too few pieces to mate, a position repeated three times and the fifty-move rule are draws. WOPR claims the last two at once.
At YOUR MOVE: type a move as its squares (E2E4, E2-E4 or E2 E4). Algebraic notation also works (NF3, EXD5, O-O, O-O-O).
To promote a pawn, type E7E8Q or E8=Q. E7E8 alone makes a queen.
The board marks the square the last move left with [] and the square it reached with <. Beside the board, TAKEN lists the pieces each side took, and CHECK shows when you are in check.
A move that is not legal gets ILLEGAL MOVE. Type RESIGN to give up.

controls.does: move by squares, from then to (E2-E4 and E2 E4 work too)
move in algebraic notation. EXD5 is a pawn capture
castle on the king's side or the queen's side (0-0 and 0-0-0 work too)
promote a pawn. E7E8 alone makes a queen
leave the game and return to WOPR

tips: WOPR looks only four half-moves ahead (three with a seed), plus any captures after that. A plan that needs several quiet moves can succeed against it. For example, build an attack on its king, or push a pawn to promote.
WOPR takes any piece it can win within that short look ahead. After each move, check that each of your pieces has a defender or is out of reach.
When you are ahead, do not repeat positions. WOPR counts a repeated position as a draw. When it is losing, it steers toward one.
For an easier game, run it with a seed (wopr chess -s 1). WOPR then looks one half-move less far ahead.

screenshots.caption: An illegal E2E5 gets ILLEGAL MOVE. Then, after E2E4 D7D5 and EXD5, WOPR's queen recaptures on D5. The board marks where it left ([]) and where it landed (<).
NC3 attacks the queen, and WOPR answers D5E6 with check. The console says CHECK. and CHECK shows beside YOU.
After O-O and G8F6: White castled, and each side moved both of its knights off its back row.
